newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sulzer Medica sees lower sales return.
newsitem.headline: Sulzer Medica sees lower sales return.

text.p: Sulzer Medica, the medical technology subsidiary of Sulzer AG that is going public in two weeks, said it expected its rate of return on sales to decline again this year before rising in 1998.
Sulzer Medica chief executive Andre Buchel said the percentage return would decline this year despite a strong first quarter, when sales rose 20 percent from a year earlier in Swiss franc terms.

"It can be assumed that 1997 will be the year with this slight decline in return on sales. We expect a positive trend starting in 1998 at the latest, not least because of sales of new products," he told a news conference.
Buchel said the decline was due to investments in expanding the sales network and in new products.
Return on sales was 19 percent in 1994 and 1995 but 18.7 percent last year, he said.
Sulzer Medica had been able to maintain its gross margins despite price pressures in the health care industry, he added.
Diversified technology group Sulzer is spinning off Sulzer Medica to raise capital for the medical unit's expansion, including through acquisitions.
Sulzer Medica will remain three-quarters held by Sulzer once shares are placed, with trading due to start in the week of July 14.
Sulzer Medica posted 1.16 billion Swiss francs in 1996 sales and employed 4,557 people.

It designs, manufactures and markets a range of implantable orthopedic and cardiovascular products. Orthopedic products accounted for 52 percent and cardiovascular products for 48 percent of 1996 sales. Europe made up 47 percent of sales and North America 40 percent. -- Zurich Newsroom, +41-1-631 7340
